notes: All twelve tools are unconditionally registered in `snapshotTools` (dist/index.js:716-727) and passed to `createServerWithTools` (dist/index.js:729-736); there are no flags, env vars or toolsets gating them.

Every tool is a thin relay over a websocket to the Browser MCP browser extension (dist/index.js:125-137, 205-211). Actual reach therefore depends on the extension's permissions for the connected tab; whether `file://` or localhost pages can be driven is not settled in this source, so the broadest (SECRET) reading is kept for the snapshot/screenshot/console tools.

`killProcessOnPort` runs `execSync` with a shell command at startup (dist/index.js:169-181, 184-190), but the port is the fixed default 9009 and is not reachable from any tool argument, so no tool gets HOSTEXEC from it.
If no extension tab is connected, tools throw `noConnectionMessage` (dist/index.js:110-118); this is an availability condition, not a capability restriction.

browser_click.rationale: `click` sends `browser_click` to the extension and then returns `captureAriaSnapshot` content, exposing the resulting page (user's session data → SECRET; attacker page text → UNTRUSTED). The click itself carries only an element reference, no agent-authored payload, so it is not itself an exfiltration channel.

browser_get_console_logs.rationale: `getConsoleLogs` returns the connected tab's console output verbatim (`consoleLogs.map((log) => JSON.stringify(log))`). Logs of an authenticated app can contain private data/tokens (SECRET) and any page script — including an attacker's — can write arbitrary strings to the console (UNTRUSTED).

browser_go_back.rationale: `goBack` is registered with snapshot=true (`goBack(true)` at line 717) and returns `captureAriaSnapshot`, i.e. the URL, title and full accessibility snapshot of whatever page the user's logged-in browser lands on: private session content (SECRET) and possibly attacker-authored page text (UNTRUSTED). No agent-supplied data leaves the host.

browser_go_forward.rationale: `goForward(true)` returns `captureAriaSnapshot` content for the resulting page — the user's authenticated browser content (SECRET) and potentially attacker-controlled page text (UNTRUSTED).

browser_hover.rationale: `hover` returns `captureAriaSnapshot` output after hovering, so page content of the connected tab reaches the agent: private authenticated content (SECRET) and attacker-authored page text (UNTRUSTED).

browser_navigate.rationale: `navigate` forwards an agent-chosen `url` over the websocket to the browser extension (`context.sendSocketMessage("browser_navigate", { url })`), so the agent can cause the user's real browser to issue a request to any attacker-chosen host, with data smuggled in the URL path/query — a SINK. It is registered as `navigate(true)` so it then calls `captureAriaSnapshot`, returning the page URL, title and accessibility tree; on an attacker page that is attacker-controlled text (UNTRUSTED), and on an authenticated/intranet/localhost/file: page it is the user's private content read with the user's browser session (SECRET).

browser_press_key.rationale: `pressKey` forwards a single key name to the extension and returns only the fixed string `Pressed key ${key}`; no page content is returned and no agent-authored payload of meaningful size leaves the host.

browser_screenshot.rationale: `screenshot` returns a PNG of the current tab into the agent context: pixels of the user's logged-in page (SECRET) and, when the tab shows attacker content, attacker-chosen rendered text/instructions (UNTRUSTED).

browser_select_option.rationale: `selectOption` sets dropdown values in the page and returns `captureAriaSnapshot` content: user's private page content (SECRET) and attacker-authored page text (UNTRUSTED). The selected values are constrained to existing option values, so it is not treated as a general exfiltration channel.

browser_snapshot.rationale: `snapshot.handle` calls `captureAriaSnapshot`, which asks the extension for `getUrl`, `getTitle` and `browser_snapshot` of the currently connected tab. That tab may be an authenticated SaaS/intranet/localhost page (SECRET) or an attacker-controlled web page whose text is injected into the agent context (UNTRUSTED).

browser_type.rationale: `type` sends agent-supplied `text` into an editable element of the live page and can press Enter (`submit` in `TypeTool`), so arbitrary agent data can be posted into an attacker-readable destination (attacker-hosted form, public comment box, search query) — SINK. It also returns `captureAriaSnapshot` content afterwards, yielding the user's authenticated page data (SECRET) and attacker-controlled page text (UNTRUSTED).

browser_wait.rationale: `wait2` only sleeps in the browser and returns a fixed confirmation string; it reads nothing and sends nothing outward.
